flashcards.q: Why is accuracy useless for fraud detection and what do you report instead?
flashcards.a: Fraud prevalence ~0.1%: predicting 'never fraud' scores 99.9% accurate. Report precision@alert-capacity, PR-AUC, $-weighted recall, and expected-cost curves (fraud losses + review cost + customer friction) at the operating threshold.

flashcards.q: Typical latency budget for real-time card authorization scoring and how it shapes architecture.
flashcards.a: ~100-150ms end-to-end, ~30-60ms for scoring: rules first (<1ms short-circuit), precomputed features from online store (<5ms reads), light model inline (~5-15ms); heavy graph/GNN signals run async post-auth for case linkage. Timeout fallback = rules-only.

flashcards.q: What does Reg B require after adverse action and by when?
flashcards.a: Specific principal reasons for the denial within 30 days (ECOA/Reg B), plus FCRA disclosures if a consumer report was used (risk-based pricing/score disclosure). CFPB Circular 2022-03: model complexity/trade secrecy is no defense - legally sufficient justification required.

flashcards.q: Distinguish disparate treatment vs disparate impact with case anchors.
flashcards.a: Treatment: intentional use of protected class (rare). Impact: neutral practice with discriminatory effect - upheld in housing/lending contexts by Texas Dept of Housing v Inclusive Communities (2015). Engineering target: selection-rate ratios (four-fifths AIR guideline) + proxy analysis.

When base rates differ across groups, calibration-within-groups is incompatible with equalizing FPR/FNR across groups. You must choose which criterion to relax, document the choice, get legal sign-off, and monitor all metrics continuously.

flashcards.q: Give concrete proxy mechanisms and why removing zip code rarely suffices.
flashcards.a: Zip encodes segregation; merchant mix encodes religious observance; network ties encode demographics. Other features absorb removed signals (leakage), so empirical re-audits typically show residual proxies persist - removal is iterative, monitored hygiene not a one-time fix.

flashcards.q: What are typical rule-based AML false-positive rates and the modern upgrade path?
flashcards.a: 90-95%+ of alerts are false positives. Upgrades: entity resolution (one actor, many accounts/devices), graph anomaly/community detection for mule networks, NLP on SAR narratives/adverse media, ML alert prioritization against analyst capacity. HSBC 2012 ($1.9B) justifies budgets; SARs due ~30 days from detection.

Global feature importance -> risk committees; local SHAP attributions -> analysts/investigations; reason codes/narratives -> regulators+customers (legally required artifacts); counterfactuals -> customers ('what would change the decision' - actionable without revealing internals). GDPR Art 22 pushes human-in-the-loop for consequential EU decisions.

flashcards.q: EU AI Act risk tiers and the key compliance dates through 2027.
flashcards.a: Tiers: prohibited / high-risk / transparency / minimal. Creditworthiness of natural persons = Annex III HIGH-RISK: prohibitions applied Feb 2 2025; GPAI obligations Aug 2 2025; high-risk obligations Aug 2 2026; embedded-product high-risk + pre-Aug-2025 GPAI models Aug 2 2027. Fines up to EUR35M or 7% global turnover.

flashcards.q: ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI RMF in one line each.
flashcards.a: ISO/IEC 42001:2023: certifiable AI management system (AIMS) on PDCA like ISO 27001, Annex controls over policy/roles/lifecycle/data/impact/third-parties. NIST AI RMF 1.0 (Jan 2023, GenAI profile Jul 2024): four functions GOVERN/MAP/MEASURE/MANAGE mapping ~1:1 onto SR 11-7 machinery.

flashcards.q: What did Apple Card/NYDFS teach about explainability?
flashcards.a: 2019 viral limit-disparity claims; NYDFS closed March 2021 finding no unlawful discrimination but criticized opacity and weak appeals. Lessons: individual explanations + appeal paths must exist before virality; distinguish product-design gaps (individual limits ignoring household context) from statistical bias.

flashcards.q: Where do LLMs legitimately operate in finance workflows today?
flashcards.a: Summarization/drafting (SAR narratives, KYC docs, disputes) with human sign-off; document extraction; triage; investigator copilots. Never binding decisions (declines, freezes, SAR filings) without deterministic systems + humans; hallucination tracked as model-risk events; EU transparency tier requires disclosing AI interaction.
